Add-ons can encapsulate certain functionality neatly for writing tools to improve your workflow or for writing utilities for others to use. While there are limits to what Python can do within Blender, there is certainly a lot that can be achieved without having to dive into Blender’s C/C++ code. The example given in the tutorial is limited, but shows the Blender API used for common tasks that you can expand on to write your own tools. Format File format for volume based simulation data (i.e. grids and particles). Uni Cache : Blender’s own caching format with some compression. Each simulation object is stored in its own .uni cache file. OpenVDB : Advanced and efficient storage format. All simulation objects (i.e. grids and particles) are stored in a single .vdb file per frame. Compression OpenVDB Only Compression method that is used when writing OpenVDB cache files. Zip : Cache files will be written with Zip compression. Effective but slower than Blosc . Blosc : Cache files will be written with Blosc compression. Multithreaded compression, similar in size and quality to Zip compression. None : Cache files will be written without any compression. Precision OpenVDB Only Precision level that is used when writing OpenVDB cache files. Full : Volumetric data (e.g. grids, particles) will be written with full precision (32-bit). Half : Volumetric data (e.g. grids, particles) will be written with half precision (16-bit). Mini : Volumetric data (e.g. grids, particles) will be written with mini float precision (8-bit) where possible. For cache data where this is not possible, 16-bit floats will be used instead. Meshes Liquids Only File format for the mesh cache files. Binary Object: Mesh data files with some compression. Object: Simple, standard data format for mesh data. Export Mantaflow Script Export the simulation as a standalone Mantaflow script when baking the scene (exported on “Bake Data”). Usually, only developers and advanced users who know how to use the Mantaflow GUI will make use of this functionality. Registering a class with Blender results in the class definition being loaded into Blender, where it becomes available alongside existing functionality. Once this class is loaded you can access it from bpy.types , using the bl_idname rather than the classes original name. Note There are some exceptions to this for class names which aren’t guarantee to be unique. In this case use: bpy.types.Struct.bl_rna_get_subclass_py() . When loading a class, Blender performs sanity checks making sure all required properties and functions are found, that properties have the correct type, and that functions have the right number of arguments. Mostly you will not need concern yourself with this but if there is a problem with the class definition it will be raised on registering: Using the function arguments def execute(self, context, spam) , will raise an exception: ValueError: expected Operator, SimpleOperator class "execute" function to have 2 args, found 3 Using bl_idname = 1 will raise: TypeError: validating class error: Operator.bl_idname expected a string type, not int Inter-Class Dependencies When customizing Blender you may want to group your own settings together, after all, they will likely have to co-exist with other scripts. To group these properties classes need to be defined, for groups within groups or collections within groups you can’t avoid having to deal with the order of registration/unregistration. For the most part using Blender as a Python module is equivalent to running a script in background-mode (passing the command-line arguments --background or -b ), however there are some differences to be aware of. Blender’s Executable Access The attribute bpy.app.binary_path defaults to an empty string. If you wish to point this to the location of a known executable you may set the value. This example searches for the binary, setting it when found: import bpy import shutil blender_bin = shutil . which ( "blender" ) if blender_bin : print ( "Found:" , blender_bin ) bpy . app . binary_path = blender_bin else : print ( "Unable to find blender!" ) Blender’s Internal Modules There are many modules included with Blender such as gpu and mathuils . It’s important that these are imported after bpy or they will not be found. Command Line Arguments Unsupported Functionality controlled by command line arguments (shown by calling blender --help aren’t accessible). Typically this isn’t such a limitation although there are some command line arguments that don’t have equivalents in Blender’s Python API ( --threads and --log for example). Note Access to these settings may be added in the future as needed. Resource Sharing (GPU) It’s possible other Python modules make use of the GPU in a way that prevents Blender/Cycles from accessing the GPU. Signal Handlers Blender’s typical signal handlers are not initialized, so there is no special handling for Control-C to cancel a render and a crash log is not written in the event of a crash. Startup and Preferences When the bpy module loads it contains the default startup scene (instead of an “empty” blend-file as you might expect), so there is a default cube, camera and light. Blender defines a number of Python types but also uses Python native types. Blender’s Python API can be split up into three categories. Native Types In simple cases returning a number or a string as a custom type would be cumbersome, so these are accessed as normal Python types. Blender float, int, boolean -> float, int, boolean Blender enumerator -> string >>> C . object . rotation_mode = 'AXIS_ANGLE' Blender enumerator (multiple) -> set of strings # Setting multiple snap targets. bpy . context . scene . tool_settings . snap_elements_base = { 'VERTEX' , 'EDGE' } # Passing as an operator argument for report types. self . report ({ 'WARNING' , 'INFO' }, "Some message!" ) Internal Types bpy.types.bpy_struct is used for Blender data-blocks and collections. Also for data that contains its own attributes: collections, meshes, bones, scenes, etc. There are two main types that wrap Blender’s data, one for data-blocks (known internally as bpy_struct ), another for properties. >>> bpy . context . object bpy.data.objects['Cube'] >>> C . scene . objects bpy.data.scenes['Scene'].objects Note that these types reference Blender’s data so modifying them is visible immediately. Mathutils Types Accessible from mathutils are vectors, quaternions, Euler angles, matrix and color types. Some attributes such as bpy.types.Object.location , bpy.types.PoseBone.rotation_euler and bpy.types.Scene.cursor_location can be accessed as special math types which can be used together and manipulated in various useful ways. Example of a matrix, vector multiplication: bpy . context . object . matrix_world @ bpy . context . object . data . verts [ 0 ] . co Note mathutils types keep a reference to Blender’s internal data so changes can be applied back. Blender’s text editor is fine for small changes and writing tests but its not full featured, for larger projects you’ll probably want to use a standalone editor or Python IDE. Editing a text file externally and having the same text open in Blender does work but isn’t that optimal so here are two ways you can use an external file from Blender. Using the following examples you’ll still need text data-block in Blender to execute, but reference an external file rather than including it directly. Executing External Scripts This is the equivalent to running the script directly, referencing a script’s path from a two line code block. filename = "/full/path/to/myscript.py" exec ( compile ( open ( filename ) . read (), filename , 'exec' )) You might want to reference a script relative to the blend-file. import bpy import os filename = os . path . join ( os . path . dirname ( bpy . data . filepath ), "myscript.py" ) exec ( compile ( open ( filename ) . read (), filename , 'exec' )) Executing Modules This example shows loading a script in as a module and executing a module function. import myscript import importlib importlib . reload ( myscript ) myscript . main () Notice that the script is reloaded every time, this forces use of the modified version, otherwise the cached one in sys.modules would be used until Blender was restarted. The important difference between this and executing the script directly is it has to call a function in the module, in this case main() but it can be any function, an advantage with this is you can pass arguments to the function from this small script which is often useful for testing different settings quickly. Running Python scripts in the text editor is useful for testing but you’ll want to extend Blender to make tools accessible like other built-in functionality. The Blender Python API allows integration for: bpy.types.Panel bpy.types.Menu bpy.types.Operator bpy.types.PropertyGroup bpy.types.KeyingSet bpy.types.RenderEngine This is intentionally limited. Currently, for more advanced features such as mesh modifiers, object types, or shader nodes, C/C++ must be used. For Python integration Blender defines methods which are common to all types. This works by creating a Python subclass of a Blender class which contains variables and functions specified by the parent class which are predefined to interface with Blender. For example: import bpy class SimpleOperator ( bpy . types . Operator ): bl_idname = "object.simple_operator" bl_label = "Tool Name" def execute ( self , context ): print ( "Hello World" ) return { 'FINISHED' } bpy . utils . register_class ( SimpleOperator ) First note that it defines a subclass as a member of bpy.types , this is common for all classes which can be integrated with Blender and is used to distinguish an Operator from a Panel when registering. Both class properties start with a bl_ prefix. This is a convention used to distinguish Blender properties from those you add yourself. Next see the execute function, which takes an instance of the operator and the current context. A common prefix is not used for functions. Lastly the register function is called, this takes the class and loads it into Blender. See Class Registration . Blender defines a number of Python types but also uses Python native types. Blender’s Python API can be split up into three categories. Native Types In simple cases returning a number or a string as a custom type would be cumbersome, so these are accessed as normal Python types. Blender float, int, boolean -> float, int, boolean Blender enumerator -> string >>> C . object . rotation_mode = 'AXIS_ANGLE' Blender enumerator (multiple) -> set of strings # Setting multiple snap targets. bpy . context . scene . tool_settings . snap_elements_base = { 'VERTEX' , 'EDGE' } # Passing as an operator argument for report types. self . report ({ 'WARNING' , 'INFO' }, "Some message!" ) Internal Types bpy.types.bpy_struct is used for Blender data-blocks and collections. Also for data that contains its own attributes: collections, meshes, bones, scenes, etc. There are two main types that wrap Blender’s data, one for data-blocks (known internally as bpy_struct ), another for properties. >>> bpy . context . object bpy.data.objects['Cube'] >>> C . scene . objects bpy.data.scenes['Scene'].objects Note that these types reference Blender’s data so modifying them is visible immediately. Mathutils Types Accessible from mathutils are vectors, quaternions, Euler angles, matrix and color types. Some attributes such as bpy.types.Object.location , bpy.types.PoseBone.rotation_euler and bpy.types.Scene.cursor_location can be accessed as special math types which can be used together and manipulated in various useful ways. Example of a matrix, vector multiplication: bpy . context . object . matrix_world @ bpy . context . object . data . verts [ 0 ] . co Note mathutils types keep a reference to Blender’s internal data so changes can be applied back. Running Python scripts in the text editor is useful for testing but you’ll want to extend Blender to make tools accessible like other built-in functionality. The Blender Python API allows integration for: bpy.types.Panel bpy.types.Menu bpy.types.Operator bpy.types.PropertyGroup bpy.types.KeyingSet bpy.types.RenderEngine This is intentionally limited. Currently, for more advanced features such as mesh modifiers, object types, or shader nodes, C/C++ must be used. For Python integration Blender defines methods which are common to all types. This works by creating a Python subclass of a Blender class which contains variables and functions specified by the parent class which are predefined to interface with Blender. For example: import bpy class SimpleOperator ( bpy . types . Operator ): bl_idname = "object.simple_operator" bl_label = "Tool Name" def execute ( self , context ): print ( "Hello World" ) return { 'FINISHED' } bpy . utils . register_class ( SimpleOperator ) First note that it defines a subclass as a member of bpy.types , this is common for all classes which can be integrated with Blender and is used to distinguish an Operator from a Panel when registering. Both class properties start with a bl_ prefix. This is a convention used to distinguish Blender properties from those you add yourself. Next see the execute function, which takes an instance of the operator and the current context. A common prefix is not used for functions. Lastly the register function is called, this takes the class and loads it into Blender. See Class Registration . {"code":"import bpy
import math
from mathutils import Vector
from pathlib import Path

# =====================
# Paths / Output
# =====================
ASSET_NAME = "det_fallback_fire_v1"
OUTPUT_DIR = f"/home/maz3ppa/projects/PlasmaDXR/build/vdb_output/{ASSET_NAME}"
RENDER_PATH = f"{OUTPUT_DIR}/{ASSET_NAME}.png"
BLEND_PATH = f"{OUTPUT_DIR}/{ASSET_NAME}.blend"
CACHE_DIR = f"{OUTPUT_DIR}/cache"

Path(OUTPUT_DIR).mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
Path(CACHE_DIR).mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

scene = bpy.context.scene

# =====================
# Helpers
# =====================
def clean_scene():
    bpy.ops.object.select_all(action='SELECT')
    bpy.ops.object.delete(use_global=False)

    # Remove leftover datablocks (best-effort)
    for datablocks in (
        bpy.data.meshes,
        bpy.data.materials,
        bpy.data.images,
        bpy.data.lights,
        bpy.data.cameras,
        bpy.data.curves,
    ):
        for block in list(datablocks):
            if block.users == 0:
                datablocks.remove(block)


def rna_set(obj, prop_name, value):
    """Set RNA property if it exists (avoids hard crashes on version differences)."""
    if hasattr(obj, prop_name):
        try:
            setattr(obj, prop_name, value)
            return True
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"WARN: Failed to set {obj.__class__.__name__}.{prop_name} = {value!r}: {e}")
            return False
    else:
        print(f"WARN: Missing RNA prop {obj.__class__.__name__}.{prop_name}")
        return False


def look_at(obj, target: Vector, up: Vector = Vector((0, 0, 1))):
    direction = (target - obj.location).normalized()
    # Blender cameras look down -Z
    rot_quat = direction.to_track_quat('-Z', 'Y')
    obj.rotation_euler = rot_quat.to_euler()


def ensure_world_black():
    if scene.world is None:
        scene.world = bpy.data.worlds.new("World")
    scene.world.use_nodes = True
    nodes = scene.world.node_tree.nodes
    bg = nodes.get('Background')
    if bg:
        bg.inputs[0].default_value = (0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0)
        bg.inputs[1].default_value = 1.0


def setup_cycles_gpu(samples=128):
    scene.render.engine = 'CYCLES'
    scene.cycles.samples = samples

    # Basic GPU enable (best-effort)
    scene.cycles.device = 'GPU'
    try:
        cprefs = bpy.context.preferences.addons['cycles'].preferences
        # Ensure devices list is populated
        if hasattr(cprefs, "get_devices"):
            cprefs.get_devices()
        if hasattr(cprefs, "devices"):
            for d in cprefs.devices:
                try:
                    d.use = True
                except Exception:
                    pass
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"WARN: Could not configure Cycles GPU devices: {e}")


def setup_volume_material(domain_obj):
    """Volume shader for Mantaflow domain (required: otherwise renders as a gray cube)."""
    mat = bpy.data.materials.new(name="VolumeShader")
    mat.use_nodes = True
    nt = mat.node_tree
    nodes = nt.nodes
    links = nt.links
    nodes.clear()

    out = nodes.new('ShaderNodeOutputMaterial')
    out.location = (500, 0)

    vol = nodes.new('ShaderNodeVolumePrincipled')
    vol.location = (250, 0)

    # density attribute -> Density (very low smoke)
    attr_density = nodes.new('ShaderNodeAttribute')
    attr_density.attribute_name = 'density'
    attr_density.attribute_type = 'GEOMETRY'
    attr_density.location = (-600, -100)

    density_mul = nodes.new('ShaderNodeMath')
    density_mul.operation = 'MULTIPLY'
    density_mul.inputs[1].default_value = 0.2
    density_mul.location = (-350, -100)

    # flame attribute -> color ramp -> Emission Color
    attr_flame = nodes.new('ShaderNodeAttribute')
    attr_flame.attribute_name = 'flame'
    attr_flame.attribute_type = 'GEOMETRY'
    attr_flame.location = (-600, 140)

    ramp = nodes.new('ShaderNodeValToRGB')
    ramp.location = (-350, 140)
    elems = ramp.color_ramp.elements
    # Keep exactly 4 elements
    while len(elems) > 4:
        elems.remove(elems[-1])
    while len(elems) < 4:
        elems.new(0.5)
    elems[0].position = 0.00
    elems[0].color = (0.0, 0.05, 0.30, 1.0)
    elems[1].position = 0.50
    elems[1].color = (0.0, 0.25, 1.00, 1.0)
    elems[2].position = 0.80
    elems[2].color = (1.0, 0.80, 0.15, 1.0)
    elems[3].position = 1.00
    elems[3].color = (1.0, 0.45, 0.00, 1.0)

    flame_strength = nodes.new('ShaderNodeMath')
    flame_strength.operation = 'MULTIPLY'
    flame_strength.inputs[1].default_value = 25.0
    flame_strength.location = (-100, 140)

    # Optional: use flame to drive blackbody intensity too
    bb_mul = nodes.new('ShaderNodeMath')
    bb_mul.operation = 'MULTIPLY'
    bb_mul.inputs[1].default_value = 2.0
    bb_mul.location = (-100, 260)

    links.new(attr_density.outputs.get('Fac'), density_mul.inputs[0])
    links.new(density_mul.outputs.get('Value'), vol.inputs.get('Density'))

    links.new(attr_flame.outputs.get('Fac'), ramp.inputs.get('Fac'))
    links.new(ramp.outputs.get('Color'), vol.inputs.get('Emission Color', vol.inputs.get('Emission')))

    links.new(attr_flame.outputs.get('Fac'), flame_strength.inputs[0])
    links.new(flame_strength.outputs.get('Value'), vol.inputs.get('Emission Strength'))

    links.new(attr_flame.outputs.get('Fac'), bb_mul.inputs[0])
    if 'Blackbody Intensity' in vol.inputs:
        links.new(bb_mul.outputs.get('Value'), vol.inputs['Blackbody Intensity'])
        vol.inputs['Blackbody Tint'].default_value = (1.0, 0.85, 0.60, 1.0)

    links.new(vol.outputs.get('Volume'), out.inputs.get('Volume'))

    if domain_obj.data.materials:
        domain_obj.data.materials[0] = mat
    else:
        domain_obj.data.materials.append(mat)


def make_burner_geometry():
    # Burner ring (brass) ~10cm diameter
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_torus_add(major_radius=0.05, minor_radius=0.006, major_segments=48, minor_segments=18)
    burner = bpy.context.active_object
    burner.name = "BurnerRing"
    burner.location = (0.0, 0.0, 0.0)

    # Simple grate: 2 crossing bars
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cube_add(size=1.0)
    bar1 = bpy.context.active_object
    bar1.name = "GrateBar1"
    bar1.scale = (0.07, 0.008, 0.004)
    bar1.location = (0.0, 0.0, 0.01)

    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cube_add(size=1.0)
    bar2 = bpy.context.active_object
    bar2.name = "GrateBar2"
    bar2.scale = (0.008, 0.07, 0.004)
    bar2.location = (0.0, 0.0, 0.01)

    # Materials
    brass = bpy.data.materials.new("Brass")
    brass.use_nodes = True
    bsdf = brass.node_tree.nodes.get("Principled BSDF")
    if bsdf:
        bsdf.inputs.get('Base Color').default_value = (0.62, 0.46, 0.18, 1.0)
        bsdf.inputs.get('Roughness').default_value = 0.35
        # 5.0 renamed "Specular" -> "Specular IOR Level"
        spec = bsdf.inputs.get('Specular IOR Level', bsdf.inputs.get('Specular'))
        if spec:
            spec.default_value = 0.5
        metallic = bsdf.inputs.get('Metallic')
        if metallic:
            metallic.default_value = 1.0

    steel = bpy.data.materials.new("Steel")
    steel.use_nodes = True
    bsdf2 = steel.node_tree.nodes.get("Principled BSDF")
    if bsdf2:
        bsdf2.inputs.get('Base Color').default_value = (0.12, 0.12, 0.12, 1.0)
        bsdf2.inputs.get('Roughness').default_value = 0.6
        met = bsdf2.inputs.get('Metallic')
        if met:
            met.default_value = 1.0

    # Hot contact glow material (thin ring)
    glow = bpy.data.materials.new("ContactGlow")
    glow.use_nodes = True
    nt = glow.node_tree
    nodes = nt.nodes
    links = nt.links
    for n in list(nodes):
        nodes.remove(n)
    out = nodes.new('ShaderNodeOutputMaterial')
    em = nodes.new('ShaderNodeEmission')
    em.inputs['Color'].default_value = (1.0, 0.45, 0.05, 1.0)
    em.inputs['Strength'].default_value = 1.2
    links.new(em.outputs['Emission'], out.inputs['Surface'])

    burner.data.materials.append(brass)
    bar1.data.materials.append(steel)
    bar2.data.materials.append(steel)

    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_torus_add(major_radius=0.05, minor_radius=0.0015, major_segments=48, minor_segments=12)
    hot = bpy.context.active_object
    hot.name = "HotContactRing"
    hot.location = (0.0, 0.0, 0.008)
    hot.data.materials.append(glow)

    return burner, [bar1, bar2], hot


def make_camera():
    bpy.ops.object.camera_add(location=(0.0, -0.23, 0.07))
    cam = bpy.context.active_object
    cam.name = "Camera"
    scene.camera = cam

    # Focus point at near edge of flame ring
    bpy.ops.object.empty_add(type='PLAIN_AXES', location=(0.05, -0.01, 0.03))
    focus = bpy.context.active_object
    focus.name = "Focus"

    look_at(cam, Vector((0.0, 0.0, 0.03)))

    cam.data.lens = 85
    cam.data.dof.use_dof = True
    cam.data.dof.focus_object = focus
    cam.data.dof.aperture_fstop = 1.8

    return cam

    # Flow emitter: thin torus (ring of ports)
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_torus_add(major_radius=0.05, minor_radius=0.002, major_segments=64, minor_segments=12)
    flow = bpy.context.active_object
    flow.name = "FireFlowRing"
    flow.location = (0.0, 0.0, 0.005)

    # Domain: cube enclosing ~20cm area
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cube_add(size=1.0, location=(0.0, 0.0, 0.06))
    domain = bpy.context.active_object
    domain.name = "FireDomain"
    domain.scale = (0.12, 0.12, 0.10)

    # Apply scale (important for fluid)
    bpy.ops.object.select_all(action='DESELECT')
    domain.select_set(True)
    bpy.context.view_layer.objects.active = domain
    bpy.ops.object.transform_apply(location=False, rotation=False, scale=True)

    bpy.ops.object.select_all(action='DESELECT')
    flow.select_set(True)
    bpy.context.view_layer.objects.active = flow
    bpy.ops.object.transform_apply(location=False, rotation=False, scale=True)

    # Fluid modifiers
    dom_mod = domain.modifiers.new(name='Fluid', type='FLUID')
    # Must set before accessing domain_settings
    rna_set(dom_mod, 'fluid_type', 'DOMAIN')

    ds = getattr(dom_mod, 'domain_settings', None)
    if ds is None:
        print("ERROR: domain_settings is None (fluid_type may not be set correctly)")
    else:
        # Core constraints (best-effort; property names may differ)
        rna_set(ds, 'domain_type', 'GAS')
        rna_set(ds, 'resolution_max', 64)
        rna_set(ds, 'use_adaptive_domain', False)
        rna_set(ds, 'vorticity', 0.25)

        # Fire tuning
        rna_set(ds, 'reaction_speed', 0.6)
        # Near-zero smoke from flames (common name in older versions)
        rna_set(ds, 'flame_smoke', 0.01)

        # Cache
        rna_set(ds, 'cache_type', 'ALL')
        rna_set(ds, 'cache_directory', CACHE_DIR)
        rna_set(ds, 'cache_frame_start', 1)
        rna_set(ds, 'cache_frame_end', 25)
        rna_set(ds, 'cache_data_format', 'OPENVDB')
        rna_set(ds, 'openvdb_compression', 'BLOSC')
        rna_set(ds, 'openvdb_precision', 'FULL')

        # Keep sim smooth/steady
        rna_set(ds, 'noise_strength', 0.0)
        rna_set(ds, 'noise_time_anim', 0.0)

    flow_mod = flow.modifiers.new(name='Fluid', type='FLUID')
    rna_set(flow_mod, 'fluid_type', 'FLOW')
    fs = getattr(flow_mod, 'flow_settings', None)
    if fs is None:
        print("ERROR: flow_settings is None (fluid_type may not be set correctly)")
    else:
        rna_set(fs, 'flow_type', 'FIRE')
        rna_set(fs, 'flow_behavior', 'INFLOW')
        rna_set(fs, 'flow_source', 'MESH')

        # Emission strength/character
        rna_set(fs, 'fuel_amount', 1.0)
        rna_set(fs, 'temperature', 1.5)

        # Initial velocity to help draft asymmetry
        rna_set(fs, 'use_initial_velocity', True)
        # Some Blender versions use velocity_coord (vector), others velocity_normal
        rna_set(fs, 'velocity_coord', (0.02, 0.0, 0.0))
        rna_set(fs, 'velocity_normal', 0.2)

        # Noise texture reference (documented in index)
        # Leave None for clean burn; if available, can be assigned a Texture datablock
        # rna_set(fs, 'noise_texture', None)

    return domain, flow, dom_mod


def make_wind():
    # Draft from left -> pushes flame +X
    try:
        bpy.ops.object.effector_add(type='WIND', location=(-0.12, 0.0, 0.05))
        wind = bpy.context.active_object
        wind.name = "LeftDraft"
        # Aim wind across the burner
        wind.rotation_euler = (0.0, 0.0, math.radians(0.0))
        if hasattr(wind, 'field'):
            rna_set(wind.field, 'strength', 0.02)
        return wind
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"WARN: could not create wind effector: {e}")
        return None


# =====================
# Build Scene
# =====================
clean_scene()

# Units & frame range
scene.frame_start = 1
scene.frame_end = 25

# Render resolution
scene.render.resolution_x = 1280
scene.render.resolution_y = 720
scene.render.film_transparent = False

ensure_world_black()
setup_cycles_gpu(samples=128)

burner, grate_bars, hot = make_burner_geometry()
cam = make_camera()

# Domain + flow
domain, flow, dom_mod = make_domain_and_flow()

# Subtle draft

    fill = bpy.context.active_object
    fill.data.energy = 5.0
    fill.data.size = 0.1
except Exception as e:
    print(f"WARN: could not add fill light: {e}")

# =====================

# =====================
bpy.context.view_layer.update()

bpy.ops.object.select_all(action='DESELECT')
domain.select_set(True)
bpy.context.view_layer.objects.active = domain

try:

        else:

except Exception as e:
    print(f"WARN: Bake failed (continuing anyway): {e}")

# =====================
# Render
# =====================
scene.frame_set(18)
scene.render.filepath = RENDER_PATH
bpy.ops.render.render(write_still=True)

# Save .blend for inspection
bpy.ops.wm.save_as_mainfile(filepath=BLEND_PATH)

{"code":"import bpy
import math
from mathutils import Vector
from pathlib import Path

# =====================
# Paths / Output
# =====================
ASSET_NAME = "det_fallback_fire_v1"
OUTPUT_DIR = f"/home/maz3ppa/projects/PlasmaDXR/build/vdb_output/{ASSET_NAME}"
RENDER_PATH = f"{OUTPUT_DIR}/{ASSET_NAME}.png"
BLEND_PATH = f"{OUTPUT_DIR}/{ASSET_NAME}.blend"
CACHE_DIR = f"{OUTPUT_DIR}/cache"

Path(OUTPUT_DIR).mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
Path(CACHE_DIR).mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

# =====================
# Tunables (match prompt constraints)
# =====================
FRAME_START = 1
FRAME_END = 25
RESOLUTION_MAX = 64
REACTION_SPEED = 0.6
SMOKE_AMOUNT = 0.01
VORTICITY = 0.25
WIND_STRENGTH = 0.02
SAMPLES = 128

scene = bpy.context.scene

# =====================
# Helpers
# =====================
def clean_scene():
    bpy.ops.object.select_all(action='SELECT')
    bpy.ops.object.delete(use_global=False)

    # Remove leftover datablocks (best-effort)
    for datablocks in (
        bpy.data.meshes,
        bpy.data.materials,
        bpy.data.images,
        bpy.data.lights,
        bpy.data.cameras,
        bpy.data.curves,
    ):
        for block in list(datablocks):
            if block.users == 0:
                datablocks.remove(block)


def look_at(obj, target: Vector):
    direction = (target - obj.location).normalized()
    rot_quat = direction.to_track_quat('-Z', 'Y')
    obj.rotation_euler = rot_quat.to_euler()


def ensure_world_black():
    if scene.world is None:
        scene.world = bpy.data.worlds.new("World")
    scene.world.use_nodes = True
    nodes = scene.world.node_tree.nodes
    bg = nodes.get('Background')
    if bg:
        bg.inputs[0].default_value = (0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0)
        bg.inputs[1].default_value = 1.0


def setup_cycles_gpu(samples=128):
    scene.render.engine = 'CYCLES'
    scene.cycles.samples = samples
    scene.cycles.device = 'GPU'

    # Best-effort device enable
    try:
        cprefs = bpy.context.preferences.addons['cycles'].preferences
        if hasattr(cprefs, "get_devices"):
            cprefs.get_devices()
        if hasattr(cprefs, "devices"):
            for d in cprefs.devices:
                try:
                    d.use = True
                except Exception:
                    pass
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"WARN: Could not configure Cycles GPU devices: {e}")


def setup_volume_material(domain_obj):
    """Volume shader for Mantaflow domain (required: otherwise renders as a gray cube)."""
    mat = bpy.data.materials.new(name="VolumeShader")
    mat.use_nodes = True
    nt = mat.node_tree
    nodes = nt.nodes
    links = nt.links
    nodes.clear()

    out = nodes.new('ShaderNodeOutputMaterial')
    out.location = (500, 0)

    vol = nodes.new('ShaderNodeVolumePrincipled')
    vol.location = (220, 0)

    # density attribute -> Density (keep low; clean burn)
    attr_density = nodes.new('ShaderNodeAttribute')
    attr_density.attribute_name = 'density'
    attr_density.attribute_type = 'GEOMETRY'
    attr_density.location = (-650, -140)

    density_mul = nodes.new('ShaderNodeMath')
    density_mul.operation = 'MULTIPLY'
    density_mul.inputs[1].default_value = 0.2
    density_mul.location = (-380, -140)

    # flame attribute -> color ramp -> Emission Color
    attr_flame = nodes.new('ShaderNodeAttribute')
    attr_flame.attribute_name = 'flame'
    attr_flame.attribute_type = 'GEOMETRY'
    attr_flame.location = (-650, 140)

    ramp = nodes.new('ShaderNodeValToRGB')
    ramp.location = (-380, 140)
    elems = ramp.color_ramp.elements
    # Keep exactly 4 elements (Blender 5.0: no elements.clear())
    while len(elems) > 4:
        elems.remove(elems[-1])
    while len(elems) < 4:
        elems.new(0.5)
    elems[0].position = 0.00
    elems[0].color = (0.0, 0.05, 0.30, 1.0)
    elems[1].position = 0.50
    elems[1].color = (0.0, 0.25, 1.00, 1.0)
    elems[2].position = 0.80
    elems[2].color = (1.0, 0.80, 0.15, 1.0)
    elems[3].position = 1.00
    elems[3].color = (1.0, 0.45, 0.00, 1.0)

    flame_strength = nodes.new('ShaderNodeMath')
    flame_strength.operation = 'MULTIPLY'
    flame_strength.inputs[1].default_value = 25.0
    flame_strength.location = (-120, 120)

    links.new(attr_density.outputs['Fac'], density_mul.inputs[0])
    if 'Density' in vol.inputs:
        links.new(density_mul.outputs['Value'], vol.inputs['Density'])

    links.new(attr_flame.outputs['Fac'], ramp.inputs['Fac'])
    # Blender 5.0: Emission socket name can vary; try both
    em_col_input = vol.inputs.get('Emission Color', vol.inputs.get('Emission'))
    if em_col_input is not None:
        links.new(ramp.outputs['Color'], em_col_input)

    links.new(attr_flame.outputs['Fac'], flame_strength.inputs[0])
    if 'Emission Strength' in vol.inputs:
        links.new(flame_strength.outputs['Value'], vol.inputs['Emission Strength'])

    links.new(vol.outputs['Volume'], out.inputs['Volume'])

    if domain_obj.data.materials:
        domain_obj.data.materials[0] = mat
    else:
        domain_obj.data.materials.append(mat)


def make_burner_geometry():
    # Burner ring (brass) ~10cm diameter
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_torus_add(major_radius=0.05, minor_radius=0.006, major_segments=48, minor_segments=18)
    burner = bpy.context.active_object
    burner.name = "BurnerRing"
    burner.location = (0.0, 0.0, 0.0)

    # Simple grate: 2 crossing bars
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cube_add(size=1.0)
    bar1 = bpy.context.active_object
    bar1.name = "GrateBar1"
    bar1.scale = (0.07, 0.008, 0.004)
    bar1.location = (0.0, 0.0, 0.01)

    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cube_add(size=1.0)
    bar2 = bpy.context.active_object
    bar2.name = "GrateBar2"
    bar2.scale = (0.008, 0.07, 0.004)
    bar2.location = (0.0, 0.0, 0.01)

    brass = bpy.data.materials.new("Brass")
    brass.use_nodes = True
    bsdf = brass.node_tree.nodes.get("Principled BSDF")
    if bsdf:
        bsdf.inputs['Base Color'].default_value = (0.62, 0.46, 0.18, 1.0)
        bsdf.inputs['Roughness'].default_value = 0.35
        spec = bsdf.inputs.get('Specular IOR Level', bsdf.inputs.get('Specular'))
        if spec:
            spec.default_value = 0.5
        if 'Metallic' in bsdf.inputs:
            bsdf.inputs['Metallic'].default_value = 1.0

    steel = bpy.data.materials.new("Steel")
    steel.use_nodes = True
    bsdf2 = steel.node_tree.nodes.get("Principled BSDF")
    if bsdf2:
        bsdf2.inputs['Base Color'].default_value = (0.12, 0.12, 0.12, 1.0)
        bsdf2.inputs['Roughness'].default_value = 0.6
        if 'Metallic' in bsdf2.inputs:
            bsdf2.inputs['Metallic'].default_value = 1.0

    glow = bpy.data.materials.new("ContactGlow")
    glow.use_nodes = True
    nt = glow.node_tree
    nodes = nt.nodes
    links = nt.links
    nodes.clear()
    out = nodes.new('ShaderNodeOutputMaterial')
    em = nodes.new('ShaderNodeEmission')
    em.inputs['Color'].default_value = (1.0, 0.45, 0.05, 1.0)
    em.inputs['Strength'].default_value = 1.2
    links.new(em.outputs['Emission'], out.inputs['Surface'])

    burner.data.materials.append(brass)
    bar1.data.materials.append(steel)
    bar2.data.materials.append(steel)

    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_torus_add(major_radius=0.05, minor_radius=0.0015, major_segments=48, minor_segments=12)
    hot = bpy.context.active_object
    hot.name = "HotContactRing"
    hot.location = (0.0, 0.0, 0.008)
    hot.data.materials.append(glow)

    return burner, [bar1, bar2], hot


def make_camera():
    bpy.ops.object.camera_add(location=(0.0, -0.23, 0.07))
    cam = bpy.context.active_object
    cam.name = "Camera"
    scene.camera = cam

    bpy.ops.object.empty_add(type='PLAIN_AXES', location=(0.05, -0.01, 0.03))
    focus = bpy.context.active_object
    focus.name = "Focus"

    look_at(cam, Vector((0.0, 0.0, 0.03)))

    cam.data.lens = 85
    cam.data.dof.use_dof = True
    cam.data.dof.focus_object = focus
    cam.data.dof.aperture_fstop = 1.8
    return cam


def make_domain_and_flow():
    # Flow emitter: thin torus (ring of ports)
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_torus_add(major_radius=0.05, minor_radius=0.002, major_segments=64, minor_segments=12)
    flow = bpy.context.active_object
    flow.name = "FireFlowRing"
    flow.location = (0.0, 0.0, 0.005)

    # Domain: cube enclosing ~20cm area
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cube_add(size=1.0, location=(0.0, 0.0, 0.06))
    domain = bpy.context.active_object
    domain.name = "FireDomain"
    domain.scale = (0.12, 0.12, 0.10)

    # Apply scale (important for fluid)
    bpy.ops.object.select_all(action='DESELECT')
    domain.select_set(True)
    bpy.context.view_layer.objects.active = domain
    bpy.ops.object.transform_apply(location=False, rotation=False, scale=True)

    bpy.ops.object.select_all(action='DESELECT')
    flow.select_set(True)
    bpy.context.view_layer.objects.active = flow
    bpy.ops.object.transform_apply(location=False, rotation=False, scale=True)

    # Fluid domain
    dom_mod = domain.modifiers.new(name='Fluid', type='FLUID')
    dom_mod.fluid_type = 'DOMAIN'  # critical ordering in Mantaflow
    ds = dom_mod.domain_settings

    # Domain settings (GAS + FIRE)
    ds.domain_type = 'GAS'
    ds.resolution_max = RESOLUTION_MAX
    ds.use_adaptive_domain = False
    ds.vorticity = VORTICITY

    # Fire tuning (clean, steady)
    ds.reaction_speed = REACTION_SPEED
    ds.flame_smoke = SMOKE_AMOUNT

    # Cache
    ds.cache_type = 'ALL'
    ds.cache_directory = CACHE_DIR
    ds.cache_frame_start = FRAME_START
    ds.cache_frame_end = FRAME_END

    # Optional cache controls (may not exist in all builds)
    for name, value in (
        ('cache_data_format', 'OPENVDB'),
        ('openvdb_compression', 'BLOSC'),
        ('openvdb_precision', 'FULL'),
    ):
        if hasattr(ds, name):
            try:
                setattr(ds, name, value)
            except Exception as e:
                print(f"WARN: could not set domain {name}={value}: {e}")

    # Documented noise controls (keep off for propane steadiness)
    ds.noise_strength = 0.0
    ds.noise_time_anim = 0.0

    # Fluid flow emitter
    flow_mod = flow.modifiers.new(name='Fluid', type='FLUID')
    flow_mod.fluid_type = 'FLOW'
    fs = flow_mod.flow_settings

    fs.flow_type = 'FIRE'
    fs.flow_behavior = 'INFLOW'
    fs.flow_source = 'MESH'

    # Strength/character
    if hasattr(fs, 'fuel_amount'):
        fs.fuel_amount = 1.0
    if hasattr(fs, 'temperature'):
        fs.temperature = 1.5

    # Initial velocity to bias draft asymmetry
    if hasattr(fs, 'use_initial_velocity'):
        fs.use_initial_velocity = True
    if hasattr(fs, 'velocity_coord'):
        fs.velocity_coord = (0.02, 0.0, 0.0)
    if hasattr(fs, 'velocity_normal'):
        fs.velocity_normal = 0.2

    return domain, flow


def make_wind():
    # Draft from left -> pushes flame +X
    try:
        bpy.ops.object.effector_add(type='WIND', location=(-0.12, 0.0, 0.05))
        wind = bpy.context.active_object
        wind.name = "LeftDraft"
        if hasattr(wind, 'field') and hasattr(wind.field, 'strength'):
            wind.field.strength = WIND_STRENGTH
        return wind
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"WARN: could not create wind effector: {e}")
        return None


# =====================
# Build Scene
# =====================
clean_scene()

scene.frame_start = FRAME_START
scene.frame_end = FRAME_END

scene.render.resolution_x = 1280
scene.render.resolution_y = 720
scene.render.film_transparent = False

ensure_world_black()
setup_cycles_gpu(samples=SAMPLES)

make_burner_geometry()
make_camera()

domain, flow = make_domain_and_flow()
setup_volume_material(domain)
make_wind()

# Dim fill light to read the stove silhouette
try:
    bpy.ops.object.light_add(type='AREA', location=(0.0, -0.15, 0.12))
    fill = bpy.context.active_object
    fill.data.energy = 5.0
    fill.data.size = 0.1
except Exception as e:
    print(f"WARN: could not add fill light: {e}")

# =====================
# Bake (best-effort)
# =====================
bpy.context.view_layer.update()

bpy.ops.object.select_all(action='DESELECT')
domain.select_set(True)
bpy.context.view_layer.objects.active = domain

try:
    with bpy.context.temp_override(active_object=domain, object=domain):
        bpy.ops.fluid.bake_all()
except Exception as e:
    print(f"WARN: Bake failed or operator unavailable (continuing): {e}")

# =====================
# Render
# =====================
scene.frame_set(18)
scene.render.filepath = RENDER_PATH
bpy.ops.render.render(write_still=True)

bpy.ops.wm.save_as_mainfile(filepath=BLEND_PATH)

{"code":"import bpy
import math
from mathutils import Vector
from pathlib import Path

# =====================
# Paths / Output
# =====================
ASSET_NAME = "det_fallback_fire_v1"
OUTPUT_DIR = f"/home/maz3ppa/projects/PlasmaDXR/build/vdb_output/{ASSET_NAME}"
FRAMES_DIR = f"{OUTPUT_DIR}/frames"
RENDER_PATH = f"{FRAMES_DIR}/{ASSET_NAME}_"  # Blender appends frame number
BLEND_PATH = f"{OUTPUT_DIR}/{ASSET_NAME}.blend"
CACHE_DIR = f"{OUTPUT_DIR}/cache"

Path(OUTPUT_DIR).mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
Path(FRAMES_DIR).mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
Path(CACHE_DIR).mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

# =====================
# Tunables (match prompt constraints)
# =====================
FRAME_START = 1
FRAME_END = 25
RESOLUTION_MAX = 64
REACTION_SPEED = 0.6  # target: medium steady gas flame
SMOKE_AMOUNT = 0.01   # near-zero
VORTICITY = 0.25      # low
WIND_STRENGTH = 0.02
SAMPLES = 128

scene = bpy.context.scene

# =====================
# Helpers
# =====================
def clean_scene():
    bpy.ops.object.select_all(action='SELECT')
    bpy.ops.object.delete(use_global=False)

    # Remove leftover datablocks (best-effort)
    for datablocks in (
        bpy.data.meshes,
        bpy.data.materials,
        bpy.data.images,
        bpy.data.lights,
        bpy.data.cameras,
        bpy.data.curves,
    ):
        for block in list(datablocks):
            if block.users == 0:
                datablocks.remove(block)


def safe_set(obj, name, value):
    """Set RNA property if present; never raises."""
    try:
        if hasattr(obj, name):
            setattr(obj, name, value)
            return True
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"WARN: failed to set {obj.__class__.__name__}.{name}={value!r}: {e}")
    return False


def safe_set_first(obj, names, value):
    for name in names:
        if safe_set(obj, name, value):
            return name
    return None


def safe_set_by_keywords(obj, include_keywords, value, exclude_keywords=(), prefer_keywords=()):
    """Heuristic fallback when Blender renames Mantaflow settings across versions.

    Scans dir(obj) and sets the first property whose name contains all include_keywords.
    """
    names = [n for n in dir(obj) if all(k in n.lower() for k in include_keywords)]
    names = [n for n in names if not any(k in n.lower() for k in exclude_keywords)]

    def score(n):
        nlow = n.lower()
        return sum(1 for k in prefer_keywords if k in nlow)

    names.sort(key=score, reverse=True)
    for n in names:
        if safe_set(obj, n, value):
            return n
    return None


def look_at(obj, target: Vector):
    direction = (target - obj.location).normalized()
    rot_quat = direction.to_track_quat('-Z', 'Y')
    obj.rotation_euler = rot_quat.to_euler()


def ensure_world_black():
    if scene.world is None:
        scene.world = bpy.data.worlds.new("World")
    # Nodes are effectively always available; avoid deprecated use_nodes flag where possible.
    try:
        scene.world.use_nodes = True
    except Exception:
        pass

    nt = scene.world.node_tree
    if nt is None:
        return
    nodes = nt.nodes
    bg = nodes.get('Background')
    if bg:
        bg.inputs[0].default_value = (0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0)
        bg.inputs[1].default_value = 1.0


def setup_cycles_gpu(samples=128):
    scene.render.engine = 'CYCLES'
    scene.cycles.samples = samples
    scene.cycles.device = 'GPU'

    # Best-effort device enable
    try:
        cprefs = bpy.context.preferences.addons['cycles'].preferences
        if hasattr(cprefs, "get_devices"):
            cprefs.get_devices()
        if hasattr(cprefs, "devices"):
            for d in cprefs.devices:
                try:
                    d.use = True
                except Exception:
                    pass
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"WARN: Could not configure Cycles GPU devices: {e}")


def setup_volume_material(domain_obj):
    """Volume shader for Mantaflow domain (required: otherwise renders as a gray cube)."""
    mat = bpy.data.materials.new(name="VolumeShader")
    try:
        mat.use_nodes = True
    except Exception:
        pass

    nt = mat.node_tree
    if nt is None:
        return

    nodes = nt.nodes
    links = nt.links
    nodes.clear()

    out = nodes.new('ShaderNodeOutputMaterial')
    out.location = (500, 0)

    vol = nodes.new('ShaderNodeVolumePrincipled')
    vol.location = (220, 0)

    # density attribute -> Density (keep low; clean burn)
    attr_density = nodes.new('ShaderNodeAttribute')
    attr_density.attribute_name = 'density'
    attr_density.attribute_type = 'GEOMETRY'
    attr_density.location = (-650, -140)

    density_mul = nodes.new('ShaderNodeMath')
    density_mul.operation = 'MULTIPLY'
    density_mul.inputs[1].default_value = 0.2
    density_mul.location = (-380, -140)

    # flame attribute -> color ramp -> Emission Color
    attr_flame = nodes.new('ShaderNodeAttribute')
    attr_flame.attribute_name = 'flame'
    attr_flame.attribute_type = 'GEOMETRY'
    attr_flame.location = (-650, 140)

    ramp = nodes.new('ShaderNodeValToRGB')
    ramp.location = (-380, 140)
    elems = ramp.color_ramp.elements
    # Keep exactly 4 elements (Blender 5.0: no elements.clear())
    while len(elems) > 4:
        elems.remove(elems[-1])
    while len(elems) < 4:
        elems.new(0.5)
    elems[0].position = 0.00
    elems[0].color = (0.0, 0.05, 0.30, 1.0)
    elems[1].position = 0.50
    elems[1].color = (0.0, 0.25, 1.00, 1.0)
    elems[2].position = 0.80
    elems[2].color = (1.0, 0.80, 0.15, 1.0)
    elems[3].position = 1.00
    elems[3].color = (1.0, 0.45, 0.00, 1.0)

    flame_strength = nodes.new('ShaderNodeMath')
    flame_strength.operation = 'MULTIPLY'
    flame_strength.inputs[1].default_value = 25.0
    flame_strength.location = (-120, 120)

    links.new(attr_density.outputs['Fac'], density_mul.inputs[0])
    if 'Density' in vol.inputs:
        links.new(density_mul.outputs['Value'], vol.inputs['Density'])

    links.new(attr_flame.outputs['Fac'], ramp.inputs['Fac'])
    em_col_input = vol.inputs.get('Emission Color', vol.inputs.get('Emission'))
    if em_col_input is not None:
        links.new(ramp.outputs['Color'], em_col_input)

    links.new(attr_flame.outputs['Fac'], flame_strength.inputs[0])
    if 'Emission Strength' in vol.inputs:
        links.new(flame_strength.outputs['Value'], vol.inputs['Emission Strength'])

    links.new(vol.outputs['Volume'], out.inputs['Volume'])

    if domain_obj.data.materials:
        domain_obj.data.materials[0] = mat
    else:
        domain_obj.data.materials.append(mat)


def make_burner_geometry():
    # Burner ring (brass) ~10cm diameter
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_torus_add(major_radius=0.05, minor_radius=0.006, major_segments=48, minor_segments=18)
    burner = bpy.context.active_object
    burner.name = "BurnerRing"
    burner.location = (0.0, 0.0, 0.0)

    # Simple grate: 2 crossing bars
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cube_add(size=1.0)
    bar1 = bpy.context.active_object
    bar1.name = "GrateBar1"
    bar1.scale = (0.07, 0.008, 0.004)
    bar1.location = (0.0, 0.0, 0.01)

    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cube_add(size=1.0)
    bar2 = bpy.context.active_object
    bar2.name = "GrateBar2"
    bar2.scale = (0.008, 0.07, 0.004)
    bar2.location = (0.0, 0.0, 0.01)

    brass = bpy.data.materials.new("Brass")
    try:
        brass.use_nodes = True
    except Exception:
        pass
    bsdf = brass.node_tree.nodes.get("Principled BSDF") if brass.node_tree else None
    if bsdf:
        bsdf.inputs['Base Color'].default_value = (0.62, 0.46, 0.18, 1.0)
        bsdf.inputs['Roughness'].default_value = 0.35
        spec = bsdf.inputs.get('Specular IOR Level', bsdf.inputs.get('Specular'))
        if spec:
            spec.default_value = 0.5
        if 'Metallic' in bsdf.inputs:
            bsdf.inputs['Metallic'].default_value = 1.0

    steel = bpy.data.materials.new("Steel")
    try:
        steel.use_nodes = True
    except Exception:
        pass
    bsdf2 = steel.node_tree.nodes.get("Principled BSDF") if steel.node_tree else None
    if bsdf2:
        bsdf2.inputs['Base Color'].default_value = (0.12, 0.12, 0.12, 1.0)
        bsdf2.inputs['Roughness'].default_value = 0.6
        if 'Metallic' in bsdf2.inputs:
            bsdf2.inputs['Metallic'].default_value = 1.0

    glow = bpy.data.materials.new("ContactGlow")
    try:
        glow.use_nodes = True
    except Exception:
        pass
    if glow.node_tree:
        nodes = glow.node_tree.nodes
        links = glow.node_tree.links
        nodes.clear()
        out = nodes.new('ShaderNodeOutputMaterial')
        em = nodes.new('ShaderNodeEmission')
        em.inputs['Color'].default_value = (1.0, 0.45, 0.05, 1.0)
        em.inputs['Strength'].default_value = 1.2
        links.new(em.outputs['Emission'], out.inputs['Surface'])

    burner.data.materials.append(brass)
    bar1.data.materials.append(steel)
    bar2.data.materials.append(steel)

    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_torus_add(major_radius=0.05, minor_radius=0.0015, major_segments=48, minor_segments=12)

{"code":"import bpy
import math
from mathutils import Vector
from pathlib import Path

# =====================
# Paths / Output
# =====================
ASSET_NAME = "det_fallback_fire_v1"
OUTPUT_DIR = f"/home/maz3ppa/projects/PlasmaDXR/build/vdb_output/{ASSET_NAME}"
FRAMES_DIR = f"{OUTPUT_DIR}/frames"
RENDER_PATH = f"{FRAMES_DIR}/{ASSET_NAME}_"  # Blender appends frame number
BLEND_PATH = f"{OUTPUT_DIR}/{ASSET_NAME}.blend"
CACHE_DIR = f"{OUTPUT_DIR}/cache"

Path(OUTPUT_DIR).mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
Path(FRAMES_DIR).mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
Path(CACHE_DIR).mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

# =====================
# Tunables (match prompt constraints)
# =====================
FRAME_START = 1
FRAME_END = 25
RESOLUTION_MAX = 64
REACTION_SPEED = 0.6  # target: medium steady gas flame
SMOKE_AMOUNT = 0.01   # near-zero
VORTICITY = 0.25      # low
WIND_STRENGTH = 0.02
SAMPLES = 128

scene = bpy.context.scene

# =====================
# Helpers
# =====================
def clean_scene():
    bpy.ops.object.select_all(action='SELECT')
    bpy.ops.object.delete(use_global=False)

    # Remove leftover datablocks (best-effort)
    for datablocks in (
        bpy.data.meshes,
        bpy.data.materials,
        bpy.data.images,
        bpy.data.lights,
        bpy.data.cameras,
        bpy.data.curves,
    ):
        for block in list(datablocks):
            if block.users == 0:
                datablocks.remove(block)


def safe_set(obj, name, value):
    """Set RNA property if present; never raises."""
    try:
        if hasattr(obj, name):
            setattr(obj, name, value)
            return True
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"WARN: failed to set {obj.__class__.__name__}.{name}={value!r}: {e}")
    return False


def safe_set_by_keywords(obj, include_keywords, value, exclude_keywords=(), prefer_keywords=()):
    """Heuristic fallback when Blender renames Mantaflow settings across versions.

    Scans dir(obj) and sets the first property whose name contains all include_keywords.
    """
    names = [n for n in dir(obj) if all(k in n.lower() for k in include_keywords)]
    names = [n for n in names if not any(k in n.lower() for k in exclude_keywords)]

    def score(n):
        nlow = n.lower()
        return sum(1 for k in prefer_keywords if k in nlow)

    names.sort(key=score, reverse=True)
    for n in names:
        if safe_set(obj, n, value):
            return n
    return None


def look_at(obj, target: Vector):
    direction = (target - obj.location).normalized()
    rot_quat = direction.to_track_quat('-Z', 'Y')
    obj.rotation_euler = rot_quat.to_euler()


def ensure_world_black():
    if scene.world is None:
        scene.world = bpy.data.worlds.new("World")

    # Nodes are effectively always available; this is deprecated but still works.
    try:
        scene.world.use_nodes = True
    except Exception:
        pass

    nt = scene.world.node_tree
    if nt is None:
        return

    nodes = nt.nodes
    bg = nodes.get('Background')
    if bg:
        bg.inputs[0].default_value = (0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0)
        bg.inputs[1].default_value = 1.0


def setup_cycles_gpu(samples=128):
    scene.render.engine = 'CYCLES'
    scene.cycles.samples = samples
    scene.cycles.device = 'GPU'

    # Best-effort device enable
    try:
        cprefs = bpy.context.preferences.addons['cycles'].preferences
        if hasattr(cprefs, "get_devices"):
            cprefs.get_devices()
        if hasattr(cprefs, "devices"):
            for d in cprefs.devices:
                try:
                    d.use = True
                except Exception:
                    pass
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"WARN: Could not configure Cycles GPU devices: {e}")


def setup_volume_material(domain_obj):
    """Volume shader for Mantaflow domain (required: otherwise renders as a gray cube)."""
    mat = bpy.data.materials.new(name="VolumeShader")
    try:
        mat.use_nodes = True
    except Exception:
        pass

    nt = mat.node_tree
    if nt is None:
        return

    nodes = nt.nodes
    links = nt.links
    nodes.clear()

    out = nodes.new('ShaderNodeOutputMaterial')
    out.location = (500, 0)

    vol = nodes.new('ShaderNodeVolumePrincipled')
    vol.location = (220, 0)

    # density attribute -> Density (keep low; clean burn)
    attr_density = nodes.new('ShaderNodeAttribute')
    attr_density.attribute_name = 'density'
    attr_density.attribute_type = 'GEOMETRY'
    attr_density.location = (-650, -140)

    density_mul = nodes.new('ShaderNodeMath')
    density_mul.operation = 'MULTIPLY'
    density_mul.inputs[1].default_value = 0.2
    density_mul.location = (-380, -140)

    # flame attribute -> color ramp -> Emission Color
    attr_flame = nodes.new('ShaderNodeAttribute')
    attr_flame.attribute_name = 'flame'
    attr_flame.attribute_type = 'GEOMETRY'
    attr_flame.location = (-650, 140)

    ramp = nodes.new('ShaderNodeValToRGB')
    ramp.location = (-380, 140)
    elems = ramp.color_ramp.elements
    # Keep exactly 4 elements (Blender 5.0: no elements.clear())
    while len(elems) > 4:
        elems.remove(elems[-1])
    while len(elems) < 4:
        elems.new(0.5)
    elems[0].position = 0.00
    elems[0].color = (0.0, 0.05, 0.30, 1.0)
    elems[1].position = 0.50
    elems[1].color = (0.0, 0.25, 1.00, 1.0)
    elems[2].position = 0.80
    elems[2].color = (1.0, 0.80, 0.15, 1.0)
    elems[3].position = 1.00
    elems[3].color = (1.0, 0.45, 0.00, 1.0)

    flame_strength = nodes.new('ShaderNodeMath')
    flame_strength.operation = 'MULTIPLY'
    flame_strength.inputs[1].default_value = 25.0
    flame_strength.location = (-120, 120)

    links.new(attr_density.outputs['Fac'], density_mul.inputs[0])
    if 'Density' in vol.inputs:
        links.new(density_mul.outputs['Value'], vol.inputs['Density'])

    links.new(attr_flame.outputs['Fac'], ramp.inputs['Fac'])
    em_col_input = vol.inputs.get('Emission Color', vol.inputs.get('Emission'))
    if em_col_input is not None:
        links.new(ramp.outputs['Color'], em_col_input)

    links.new(attr_flame.outputs['Fac'], flame_strength.inputs[0])
    if 'Emission Strength' in vol.inputs:
        links.new(flame_strength.outputs['Value'], vol.inputs['Emission Strength'])

    links.new(vol.outputs['Volume'], out.inputs['Volume'])

    if domain_obj.data.materials:
        domain_obj.data.materials[0] = mat
    else:
        domain_obj.data.materials.append(mat)


def make_burner_geometry():
    # Burner ring (brass) ~10cm diameter
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_torus_add(major_radius=0.05, minor_radius=0.006, major_segments=48, minor_segments=18)
    burner = bpy.context.active_object
    burner.name = "BurnerRing"
    burner.location = (0.0, 0.0, 0.0)

    # Simple grate: 2 crossing bars
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cube_add(size=1.0)
    bar1 = bpy.context.active_object
    bar1.name = "GrateBar1"
    bar1.scale = (0.07, 0.008, 0.004)
    bar1.location = (0.0, 0.0, 0.01)

    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cube_add(size=1.0)
    bar2 = bpy.context.active_object
    bar2.name = "GrateBar2"
    bar2.scale = (0.008, 0.07, 0.004)
    bar2.location = (0.0, 0.0, 0.01)

    brass = bpy.data.materials.new("Brass")
    try:
        brass.use_nodes = True
    except Exception:
        pass
    bsdf = brass.node_tree.nodes.get("Principled BSDF") if brass.node_tree else None
    if bsdf:
        bsdf.inputs['Base Color'].default_value = (0.62, 0.46, 0.18, 1.0)
        bsdf.inputs['Roughness'].default_value = 0.35
        spec = bsdf.inputs.get('Specular IOR Level', bsdf.inputs.get('Specular'))
        if spec:
            spec.default_value = 0.5
        if 'Metallic' in bsdf.inputs:
            bsdf.inputs['Metallic'].default_value = 1.0

    steel = bpy.data.materials.new("Steel")
    try:
        steel.use_nodes = True
    except Exception:
        pass
    bsdf2 = steel.node_tree.nodes.get("Principled BSDF") if steel.node_tree else None
    if bsdf2:
        bsdf2.inputs['Base Color'].default_value = (0.12, 0.12, 0.12, 1.0)
        bsdf2.inputs['Roughness'].default_value = 0.6
        if 'Metallic' in bsdf2.inputs:
            bsdf2.inputs['Metallic'].default_value = 1.0

    glow = bpy.data.materials.new("ContactGlow")
    try:
        glow.use_nodes = True
    except Exception:
        pass
    if glow.node_tree:
        nodes = glow.node_tree.nodes
        links = glow.node_tree.links
        nodes.clear()
        out = nodes.new('ShaderNodeOutputMaterial')
        em = nodes.new('ShaderNodeEmission')
        em.inputs['Color'].default_value = (1.0, 0.45, 0.05, 1.0)
        em.inputs['Strength'].default_value = 1.2
        links.new(em.outputs['Emission'], out.inputs['Surface'])

    burner.data.materials.append(brass)
    bar1.data.materials.append(steel)
    bar2.data.materials.append(steel)

    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_torus_add(major_radius=0.05, minor_radius=0.0015, major_segments=48, minor_segments=12)
    hot = bpy.context.active_object
    hot.name = "HotContactRing"
    hot.location = (0.0, 0.0, 0.008)
    hot.data.materials.append(glow)

    return burner, [bar1, bar2], hot


def make_camera():
    bpy.ops.object.camera_add(location=(0.0, -0.23, 0.07))
    cam = bpy.context.active_object
    cam.name = "Camera"
    scene.camera = cam

    bpy.ops.object.empty_add(type='PLAIN_AXES', location=(0.05, -0.01, 0.03))
    focus = bpy.context.active_object
    focus.name = "Focus"

    look_at(cam, Vector((0.0, 0.0, 0.03)))

    cam.data.lens = 85
    cam.data.dof.use_dof = True
    cam.data.dof.focus_object = focus
    cam.data.dof.aperture_fstop = 1.8
    return cam


def configure_domain_settings(ds):
    # Cache settings (cache_* are referenced for FluidDomainSettings in Blender 5.0 docs index)
    safe_set(ds, 'cache_type', 'ALL')
    safe_set(ds, 'cache_directory', CACHE_DIR)
    safe_set(ds, 'cache_frame_start', FRAME_START)
    safe_set(ds, 'cache_frame_end', FRAME_END)
    safe_set(ds, 'cache_data_format', 'OPENVDB')

    # Noise controls (documented in index as FluidDomainSettings.noise_strength/noise_time_anim)
    safe_set(ds, 'noise_strength', 0.0)
    safe_set(ds, 'noise_time_anim', 0.0)

    # Explicit assignments for common settings (guarded: never crash)
    try:
        ds.domain_type = 'GAS'
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"WARN: ds.domain_type not set: {e}")

    try:
        ds.resolution_max = RESOLUTION_MAX
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"WARN: ds.resolution_max not set: {e}")
        safe_set_by_keywords(ds, include_keywords=('resolution',), value=RESOLUTION_MAX, exclude_keywords=('preview',), prefer_keywords=('max',))

    try:
        ds.use_adaptive_domain = False
    except Exception:
        pass

    try:
        ds.vorticity = VORTICITY
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"WARN: ds.vorticity not set: {e}")
        safe_set_by_keywords(ds, include_keywords=('vortic',), value=VORTICITY)

    # Reaction speed: ds.reaction_speed does not exist in Blender 5.0 (runtime error)
    # Find the closest setting by keywords.
    prop = safe_set_by_keywords(ds, include_keywords=('reaction',), value=REACTION_SPEED, prefer_keywords=('speed', 'rate'))
    if prop is None:
        prop = safe_set_by_keywords(ds, include_keywords=('burn',), value=REACTION_SPEED, prefer_keywords=('rate', 'speed'))
    print(f"INFO: reaction-speed property set via: {prop}")

    # Smoke amount from flame (near-zero)
    prop = None
    # Try common-looking name first, but don't crash if absent.
    try:
        ds.flame_smoke = SMOKE_AMOUNT
        prop = 'flame_smoke'
    except Exception:
        prop = safe_set_by_keywords(ds, include_keywords=('smoke',), value=SMOKE_AMOUNT, exclude_keywords=('use_', 'cache_'), prefer_keywords=('flame', 'amount', 'density'))
    print(f"INFO: smoke-amount property set via: {prop}")


def configure_flow_settings(fs):
    # Explicit assignments (guarded)
    for name, value in (
        ('flow_type', 'FIRE'),
        ('flow_behavior', 'INFLOW'),
        ('flow_source', 'MESH'),
        ('fuel_amount', 1.0),
        ('temperature', 1.5),
        ('use_initial_velocity', True),
        ('velocity_coord', (0.02, 0.0, 0.0)),
        ('velocity_normal', 0.2),
    ):
        safe_set(fs, name, value)


def make_domain_and_flow():
    # Flow emitter: thin torus (ring of ports)
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_torus_add(major_radius=0.05, minor_radius=0.002, major_segments=64, minor_segments=12)
    flow = bpy.context.active_object
    flow.name = "FireFlowRing"
    flow.location = (0.0, 0.0, 0.005)

    # Domain: cube enclosing ~20cm area
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cube_add(size=1.0, location=(0.0, 0.0, 0.06))
    domain = bpy.context.active_object
    domain.name = "FireDomain"
    domain.scale = (0.12, 0.12, 0.10)

    # Apply scale (important for fluid)
    bpy.ops.object.select_all(action='DESELECT')
    domain.select_set(True)
    bpy.context.view_layer.objects.active = domain
    bpy.ops.object.transform_apply(location=False, rotation=False, scale=True)

    bpy.ops.object.select_all(action='DESELECT')
    flow.select_set(True)
    bpy.context.view_layer.objects.active = flow
    bpy.ops.object.transform_apply(location=False, rotation=False, scale=True)

    # Fluid domain
    dom_mod = domain.modifiers.new(name='Fluid', type='FLUID')
    # Critical ordering: set fluid_type before accessing domain_settings
    safe_set(dom_mod, 'fluid_type', 'DOMAIN')
    ds = getattr(dom_mod, 'domain_settings', None)
    if ds is None:
        raise RuntimeError("domain_settings is None; Fluid modifier may not be configured as DOMAIN")
    configure_domain_settings(ds)

    # Fluid flow emitter
    flow_mod = flow.modifiers.new(name='Fluid', type='FLUID')
    safe_set(flow_mod, 'fluid_type', 'FLOW')
    fs = getattr(flow_mod, 'flow_settings', None)
    if fs is None:
        raise RuntimeError("flow_settings is None; Fluid modifier may not be configured as FLOW")
    configure_flow_settings(fs)

    return domain, flow


def make_wind():
    # Draft from left -> pushes flame +X
    try:
        bpy.ops.object.effector_add(type='WIND', location=(-0.12, 0.0, 0.05))
        wind = bpy.context.active_object
        wind.name = "LeftDraft"
        if hasattr(wind, 'field') and hasattr(wind.field, 'strength'):
            wind.field.strength = WIND_STRENGTH
        return wind
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"WARN: could not create wind effector: {e}")
        return None


# =====================

# =====================
clean_scene()

scene.frame_start = FRAME_START
scene.frame_end = FRAME_END

scene.render.resolution_x = 1280
scene.render.resolution_y = 720
scene.render.film_transparent = False

# Output sequence settings
scene.render.image_settings.file_format = 'PNG'
scene.render.filepath = RENDER_PATH
scene.render.use_file_extension = True

ensure_world_black()
setup_cycles_gpu(samples=SAMPLES)

make_burner_geometry()
make_camera()

domain, flow = make_domain_and_flow()
setup_volume_material(domain)
make_wind()

# Dim fill light to read the stove silhouette

    bpy.ops.object.light_add(type='AREA', location=(0.0, -0.15, 0.12))
    fill = bpy.context.active_object
    fill.data.energy = 5.0
    fill.data.size = 0.1
except Exception as e:
    print(f"WARN: could not add fill light: {e}")

# =====================
# Bake (best-effort)
# =====================

bpy.ops.object.select_all(action='DESELECT')
domain.select_set(True)
bpy.context.view_layer.objects.active = domain

try:
    with bpy.context.temp_override(active_object=domain, object=domain):
        bpy.ops.fluid.bake_all()
except Exception as e:
    print(f"WARN: Bake failed or operator unavailable (continuing): {e}")

# =====================
# Render Frames 1-25
# =====================
scene.frame_set(FRAME_START)

bpy.ops.render.render(animation=True)

# Save .blend for inspection
bpy.ops.wm.save_as_mainfile(filepath=BLEND_PATH)

Blender defines a number of Python types but also uses Python native types. Blender’s Python API can be split up into three categories. Native Types In simple cases returning a number or a string as a custom type would be cumbersome, so these are accessed as normal Python types. Blender float, int, boolean -> float, int, boolean Blender enumerator -> string >>> C . object . rotation_mode = 'AXIS_ANGLE' Blender enumerator (multiple) -> set of strings # Setting multiple snap targets. bpy . context . scene . tool_settings . snap_elements_base = { 'VERTEX' , 'EDGE' } # Passing as an operator argument for report types. self . report ({ 'WARNING' , 'INFO' }, "Some message!" ) Internal Types bpy.types.bpy_struct is used for Blender data-blocks and collections. Also for data that contains its own attributes: collections, meshes, bones, scenes, etc. There are two main types that wrap Blender’s data, one for data-blocks (known internally as bpy_struct ), another for properties. >>> bpy . context . object bpy.data.objects['Cube'] >>> C . scene . objects bpy.data.scenes['Scene'].objects Note that these types reference Blender’s data so modifying them is visible immediately. Mathutils Types Accessible from mathutils are vectors, quaternions, Euler angles, matrix and color types. Some attributes such as bpy.types.Object.location , bpy.types.PoseBone.rotation_euler and bpy.types.Scene.cursor_location can be accessed as special math types which can be used together and manipulated in various useful ways. Example of a matrix, vector multiplication: bpy . context . object . matrix_world @ bpy . context . object . data . verts [ 0 ] . co Note mathutils types keep a reference to Blender’s internal data so changes can be applied back. Blender defines a number of Python types but also uses Python native types. Blender’s Python API can be split up into three categories. Native Types In simple cases returning a number or a string as a custom type would be cumbersome, so these are accessed as normal Python types. Blender float, int, boolean -> float, int, boolean Blender enumerator -> string >>> C . object . rotation_mode = 'AXIS_ANGLE' Blender enumerator (multiple) -> set of strings # Setting multiple snap targets. bpy . context . scene . tool_settings . snap_elements_base = { 'VERTEX' , 'EDGE' } # Passing as an operator argument for report types. self . report ({ 'WARNING' , 'INFO' }, "Some message!" ) Internal Types bpy.types.bpy_struct is used for Blender data-blocks and collections. Also for data that contains its own attributes: collections, meshes, bones, scenes, etc. There are two main types that wrap Blender’s data, one for data-blocks (known internally as bpy_struct ), another for properties. >>> bpy . context . object bpy.data.objects['Cube'] >>> C . scene . objects bpy.data.scenes['Scene'].objects Note that these types reference Blender’s data so modifying them is visible immediately. Mathutils Types Accessible from mathutils are vectors, quaternions, Euler angles, matrix and color types. Some attributes such as bpy.types.Object.location , bpy.types.PoseBone.rotation_euler and bpy.types.Scene.cursor_location can be accessed as special math types which can be used together and manipulated in various useful ways. Example of a matrix, vector multiplication: bpy . context . object . matrix_world @ bpy . context . object . data . verts [ 0 ] . co Note mathutils types keep a reference to Blender’s internal data so changes can be applied back.
